title: Finance and Legal Playbook: Budgeting, Procurement, Contracts, Revenue Recognition and Billing (2026)
author: Maya Chen
summary: Consolidated operational playbook for budgeting and forecasting, contracts and legal process, procurement procedures, and revenue recognition and billing policies at Redwood Inference.
content:
Overview
This playbook documents standardized procedures for: annual budgeting and rolling forecasts; contract intake, review, and signature; procurement and supplier onboarding; and revenue recognition and billing aligned to ASC 606. It is the operational reference for finance, legal, procurement, product, and engineering stakeholders.

Scope and principles
- Applies to all entities in North America and Europe. APAC-specific requirements are in the regional appendix.
- Principles: clear ownership, predictability, compliance-first, and minimal friction through standard templates and preferred vendors.

Roles and ownership
- Finance (Budgeting and RevRec): Maya Chen \u2014 Director, Finance. Owns budgeting cadence, monthly close, and revenue recognition execution.
- Legal: Oliver Hayes \u2014 General Counsel. Owns contract templates, risk assessment, and signature authority.
- Procurement: Priya Kapoor \u2014 Head of Procurement. Owns vendor onboarding, PO issuance, and supplier payments.
- Product and Engineering Owners: Provide forecast inputs for cloud, Dedicated, and Private product lines.

1) Budgeting and forecasting
Cadence and deliverables:
1. Annual budget (planning window Oct to Dec): department budgets, headcount plan, capital requests; CFO sign-off by Dec 31.
2. Quarterly rolling forecast: submitted at quarter start with variance commentary.
3. Monthly close and ad hoc reforecast if variance >5% of quarterly run rate.

Required forecast inputs:
- Revenue by product line (Hosted API, Dedicated, Private, Add-ons) with ARR and one-time items.
- Committed customer contracts, renewals, churn assumptions.
- Capacity commitments for Dedicated GPUs and utilization.
- Headcount plan and timing.
- Planned capital and vendor commitments.

Approval thresholds (reference):
- Amount <= 5,000 USD: manager approval.
- Amount 5,001 to 50,000 USD: department head plus finance reviewer.
- Amount 50,001 to 250,000 USD: VP Finance plus procurement.
- Amount > 250,000 USD: CFO, Legal, and Procurement Committee; notify Board if runway impacted.
Note: multi-year commitments require legal and finance review regardless of amount.

2) Contracts and legal process
Contract types: MSA, SOW, DPA, NDA, Reseller Agreement, Professional Services Agreement, Cloud Hosting Agreement.
Standard lifecycle:
1. Intake: submit contract via the Contract Intake form. Include owner, deal value, term, and non-standard clauses.
2. Triage: Legal assigns risk level and reviewers.
3. Template and redline: use approved template where possible. Low-risk target response 3 business days; medium risk 7 business days.
4. Commercial approval: Finance verifies revenue model and billing terms.
5. Signature: follow signature matrix. VP Sales can sign MSAs up to 1M USD ARR impact; CFO required above.
6. Post-signature: store executed contract in the repository and create revenue schedule in RevRec system.

Contract review checklist for non-standard terms:
- Data processing and residency requirements.
- Indemnity and liability caps (default cap = total fees paid in prior 12 months; exceptions require GC approval).
- IP ownership and licensing.
- Export controls and sanctions compliance.
- Third-party redistribution or sublicensing clauses.

Signature authority summary:
- Managers: NDAs and low-value vendor agreements up to 10,000 USD.
- VPs: MSAs and SOWs up to 1,000,000 USD ARR impact.
- CFO/GC: strategic contracts, >1,000,000 USD, or non-standard liability or data terms.

3) Procurement procedures
Procurement categories:
- Category A (Strategic): hardware, Dedicated GPU suppliers, long-term cloud commitments. RFP recommended.
- Category B (Platform and SaaS): observability, security, monitoring. Use preferred vendors where possible.
- Category C (Operational): office supplies and small tools. Expedited PO.

Standard flow:
1. Requisition: requestor submits requisition with justification and cost center.
2. Sourcing: procurement solicits bids; Category A requires three bids unless exception documented.
3. Risk assessment: Security and Finance review for Category A and B vendors.
4. PO issuance: procurement issues PO after approvals.
5. Delivery and acceptance: requestor confirms receipt and acceptance.
6. Invoice and payment: AP processes invoice against PO. Standard payment terms Net30 unless negotiated.

Supplier onboarding checklist:
- Completed supplier profile and tax forms.
- Insurance certificates where required.
- Data processing addendum if vendor handles customer data.
- Payment and contact information.

Preferred vendor examples: Nimbus Compute (GPU hardware), AWS and GCP (cloud), SentinelSim (security tooling).

4) Revenue recognition and billing
Policy overview: follow ASC 606 principles. Recognize revenue when performance obligations are satisfied and allocate transaction price by standalone selling price.
Revenue types and treatments:
- Subscription (Hosted API, Dedicated reservations): ratable recognition over service period. Annual prepayments recorded as deferred revenue and amortized monthly.
- Professional services: percentage-of-completion when milestones map to transfer of control; otherwise upon completion.
- Hardware: recognize at delivery and customer acceptance.
- Credits and discounts: contra-revenue; material credits (>5% of contract value) require Finance approval.

Billing and invoicing:
- Standard terms Net30. Enterprise terms Net45 or Net60 subject to credit review.
- Billing cycles: monthly in arrears for metered usage; Dedicated typically billed monthly with true-ups; Private deals may include upfront setup fees.
- All invoices generated in the billing system and archived in Finance shared storage.

Monthly revenue close checklist:
- Confirm executed contracts and effective dates.
- Validate billable usage and committed capacities.
- Reconcile deferred revenue roll-forward.
- Post reversing entries for cancellations and refunds.

Disputes and credits:
- Customers must raise disputes within 30 days. Disputes >90 days require VP Sales and Finance approval to adjust.
- Credits issued after Finance and Sales approval. Credits over 50,000 USD require CFO sign-off.

Special considerations for Dedicated and Private offerings:
- Dedicated term commitments require deferred revenue schedules and capacity-utilization ledgers maintained by Finance.
- Private/on-prem deals must allocate revenue between hardware and support in the SOW.

Operational SLAs and targets
- Contract turnaround: low-risk MSAs target 10 business days; medium risk 20 business days. Tracked in Contract Tracker dashboard.
- Procurement RFP targets: Category A 30 days; Category B 10 days.
- AR aging: weekly review of receivables >90 days with escalation to VP Sales and Treasury.

Exceptions and change control
- Deviations from playbook require Exceptions Log entry and approval by CFO and GC.
- Emergency procurements require post-facto documentation and retroactive approvals within 5 business days.
